boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten no-purchase outings spanning Gettysburg College galleries, library collections, and the freely accessible battlefield landscape nearby.

cards.title: Browse the Latest Gallery Show
cards.subtitle: Free exhibitions inside Schmucker Hall
cards.notes: Bring a friend to compare interpretations of the current Main Gallery and Project Space exhibitions during posted public hours.
cards.short_summary: A free campus art outing with rotating exhibitions and two distinct gallery spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Gettysburg College states that Schmucker Art Gallery is free and open to the public Tuesday through Saturday, 10 a.m.–4 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public Tuesday–Saturday, 10 a.m.–4 p.m.; check the gallery page for closures and exhibition dates.

cards.title: Follow the Library Exhibit Trail
cards.subtitle: Displays spread through Musselman Library
cards.notes: Start on the main floor, then look through the Apse, stairwell, Browsing Room, and other listed exhibit areas together.
cards.short_summary: A self-paced circuit of curriculum-inspired displays distributed around the library.
cards.evidence_claim: Gettysburg College identifies multiple exhibit venues throughout Musselman Library and states that exhibit events are free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Other Exhibits & Events | Musselman Library Exhibits & Events
cards.access_notes: Use current library hours and observe visitor-access rules; listed exhibit events are free and open to the public.

cards.title: Explore the Reading Room Exhibits
cards.subtitle: Rotating displays from Gettysburg College collections
cards.notes: Visit with a classmate, study the current cases, and ask staff which manuscripts, photographs, or maps connect to the display.
cards.short_summary: A public reading room pairing rotating exhibits with primary-source collections.
cards.evidence_claim: Gettysburg College says Special Collections has rotating Reading Room exhibits and is open to the public Monday through Friday, 1–5 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Open to the public Monday–Friday, 1–5 p.m.; consult the official page before visiting for exceptions or appointment guidance.

cards.title: Walk the Battlefield Grounds
cards.subtitle: Open landscapes and monuments at Gettysburg National Military Park
cards.notes: Choose one marked section, carry water, and pause at waysides and monuments rather than trying to cover the entire park at once.
cards.short_summary: A flexible outdoor history walk across the freely accessible battlefield landscape.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service states that the Gettysburg battlefield is free to visit and open daily, weather permitting.
cards.source_title: Fees & Passes - Gettysburg National Military Park
cards.access_notes: Battlefield grounds are generally open from 30 minutes before sunrise until 30 minutes after sunset, weather permitting.

cards.title: Take the National Cemetery Walk
cards.subtitle: A reflective route through the Soldiers’ National Cemetery
cards.notes: Download the NPS walking tour, keep voices low, and follow its five stops through the cemetery’s memorial landscape.
cards.short_summary: A respectful, self-guided walk through the setting associated with the Gettysburg Address.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service says there is no entrance fee for Gettysburg National Cemetery and provides a self-guided cemetery walking tour.
cards.source_title: Frequently Asked Questions - Gettysburg National Military Park
cards.access_notes: No entrance fee; cemetery grounds are open from 30 minutes before sunrise until 30 minutes after sunset.

cards.entity_name: Gettysburg National Military Park Museum & Visitor Center
cards.title: Plan a Battlefield Day at the Visitor Center
cards.subtitle: Free entry to the park’s orientation hub
cards.notes: Pick up the park brochure, compare routes with friends, and use the information desk before starting a free battlefield outing.
cards.short_summary: A no-cost planning stop for maps, route advice, and battlefield orientation.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service states that the Visitor Center building is free to enter and that a park map and brochure are available there.
cards.source_title: Visitor Centers - Gettysburg National Military Park
cards.access_notes: The building is free to enter; the museum, film, and Cyclorama require paid tickets, so keep this hang to the free areas and information desk.

cards.title: Walk the Little Round Top Route
cards.subtitle: A self-guided summit outing south of campus
cards.notes: Use the NPS app’s Little Round Top route, stay on designated paths, and allow extra time for uneven ground and monument stops.
cards.short_summary: A free, app-supported walk around one of the battlefield’s named elevations.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service provides a 20-to-90-minute Little Round Top walking or hiking tour, and its official directions page lists the site’s parking fee as $0.
cards.access_notes: No admission or parking charge is listed; use designated paths and confirm current weather, parking, and site conditions before leaving.

cards.entity_name: Gettysburg National Military Park Ranger Programs
cards.title: Join a Free Ranger Walk
cards.subtitle: Seasonal guided hikes, walks, and talks
cards.notes: Check the day’s calendar, choose a topic and meeting point, then arrive with water and footwear suited to the listed route.
cards.short_summary: A guided group outing that adds ranger interpretation without an admission charge.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service states that its 2026 summer ranger programs are free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: All listed 2026 summer programs are free; schedules can change, and severe heat or storm warnings may modify or cancel programs.

cards.title: Share the 16-Stop Auto Tour
cards.subtitle: A self-directed circuit using the official park brochure
cards.notes: Carpool if a vehicle is already available, assign one friend to navigate, and rotate readers at the marked battlefield stops.
cards.short_summary: A choose-your-own-pace circuit connecting sixteen official battlefield tour stops.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service provides a free park brochure showing a sixteen-stop self-guided Auto Tour, and it charges no fee to drive through the park.
cards.source_title: Visitor Centers - Gettysburg National Military Park
cards.access_notes: The tour has no admission charge, but participants must supply their own transportation; fuel or vehicle costs are not included.

cards.title: Host a Battlefield Watch-Along
cards.subtitle: An online ranger-led tour for a dorm or study lounge
cards.notes: Open the sixteen-stop tour on a shared screen, choose a few locations, and pause between videos to compare observations.
cards.short_summary: A free indoor group activity built from ranger videos covering official auto-tour stops.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service identifies its Gettysburg Battlefield Virtual Tour as free and available online to visitors anywhere.
cards.source_title: Gettysburg National Military Park Launches Virtual Tour of the Battlefield
cards.access_notes: Free online access; an internet connection and viewing device are needed, but no admission or purchase is required.

warnings: The Visitor Center’s free-access areas exclude the paid museum, film, and Cyclorama experience.
The self-guided auto tour has no park fee, but users need access to their own transportation.
Ranger programs are seasonal and weather-dependent; verify the official calendar before departing.
